introduction.value: Test suite for ChibiOS/VFS. The purpose of this suite is to verify the VFS infrastructure and drivers, starting with the path handling primitives used by the root driver.

description.value: The path normalization and absolute-path construction primitives are tested independently of a file system driver.
Absolute paths are normalized by removing redundant separators and resolving dot components.
The root path remains unchanged.

code.value: test_assert(vfs_test_path_normalizes("/", "/"), "root path normalization failed");

description.value: Repeated separators collapse to the root path.

code.value: test_assert(vfs_test_path_normalizes("////", "/"), "separator normalization failed");

description.value: Redundant separators and dot components are resolved.

code.value: test_assert(vfs_test_path_normalizes("/a//b/./c/../d/", "/a/b/d"), "component normalization failed");

description.value: Parent components cannot move above the root.

code.value: test_assert(vfs_test_path_normalizes("/../../a", "/a"), "root boundary normalization failed");

description.value: Only exact dot and dot-dot components are special; names beginning with dots are retained.
Dot-prefixed names are preserved.
A trailing dot component is removed.

code.value: test_assert(vfs_test_path_normalizes("/.", "/"), "dot component normalization failed");

description.value: A parent component at the root is removed.

code.value: test_assert(vfs_test_path_normalizes("/..", "/"), "root parent normalization failed");

description.value: Repeated parent traversal stops at the root.

code.value: test_assert(vfs_test_path_normalizes("/a/../..", "/"), "repeated parent normalization failed");

description.value: The source and destination may refer to the same buffer.
A path is normalized in its source buffer.
Relative paths are combined with a current directory, while absolute paths are normalized directly.
A relative parent path is resolved against the current directory.
Parent traversal stops at the root.
An absolute input ignores the current directory and is normalized.
Invalid relative inputs and insufficient output buffers are rejected, while an exactly sized buffer succeeds.
Path normalization rejects a relative input.

code.value: n = vfs_path_normalize(buf, "relative/path", sizeof buf); test_assert(n == (size_t)0, "relative path accepted");

description.value: Absolute-path construction rejects a relative current directory.

code.value: n = vfs_path_make_absolute(buf, "path", sizeof buf, "relative"); test_assert(n == (size_t)0, "relative current directory accepted");

description.value: An exactly sized output buffer succeeds.
A buffer without room for the terminator is rejected.

code.value: n = vfs_path_normalize(small, "/abc", sizeof small); test_assert(n == (size_t)0, "undersized buffer accepted");

description.value: A long normalized path exceeding the output buffer is rejected.

code.value: n = vfs_path_normalize(buf, "/123456789012345", sizeof buf); test_assert(n == (size_t)0, "long path overflow accepted");

description.value: A combined current directory and relative path that exceeds the output buffer is rejected.
The absolute-path file system interface is tested using a minimal object derived directly from vfs_fs_c.
All file system operations dispatch through a vfs_fs_c object that has no process-aware driver interface.
Stat dispatches through the file system VMT.
Directory open dispatches through the file system VMT.
File open dispatches its path and flags through the file system VMT.
Unlink dispatches through the file system VMT.
Rename dispatches both paths through the file system VMT.
Directory creation dispatches its path and mode through the file system VMT.
Directory removal dispatches through the file system VMT.
The generic read-only open falls back from a file to a directory.
The generic writable open does not open a directory after the file system reports one.
